author: WP01
summary: Describes how the book was produced (AI-assisted, revision-bounded) and defines its evidence labels, from source-proven to blocked/unsupported/not attempted, as coordinates rather than a ladder. The production and PDF notes are book narrative; the evidence vocabulary is current, useful methodology that the site used only implicitly, so it now has a table on the compatibility and evidence page.

sections.heading: Evidence labels used in this edition

concepts.text: The edition was assembled with extensive AI-agent assistance against pinned repositories; AI output was not treated as technical authority and responsibility stays with the named human author.
concepts.note: Book production note; by brief not reproduced.

concepts.text: Claims are revision-bounded: CNA behaviour is described at one development snapshot (the earlier tag is not an alias for it), sibling behaviour at the siblings' own revisions, and executed results also name their configuration and host.

target.evidence: methodology; applied on the ecosystem page's revision table

concepts.text: Automated source scans, builds, PDF checks and review passes reduce drift but cannot make a changing codebase timeless; later editions should correct stale statements.
concepts.note: Book maintenance statement; the site's equivalent is development/maintenance.html (maintenance and pin policy).

concepts.section: Evidence labels used in this edition
concepts.text: Source-proven means a reachable implementation, fallback, refusal or absence was established from the pinned source with no build or execution implied; compile-proven means names, signatures, includes, templates and link closure were exercised in a named configuration.

concepts.section: Evidence labels used in this edition
concepts.text: Runtime-observed means the named executable path ran and produced the recorded state; renderer-engaged means the intended family and its native or translation route executed rather than a substitute or an early skip.

concepts.section: Evidence labels used in this edition
concepts.text: Oracle-compared means compared with an identified authority under a stated normalisation or tolerance; pixel-verified means selected pixels or a frame were compared at a stated readback boundary, renderer, host and tolerance.

concepts.section: Evidence labels used in this edition
concepts.text: Manually observed means a person inspected the result without a retained discriminating verdict; historically recorded means a dated project artifact reports a result that was not re-run.

concepts.section: Evidence labels used in this edition
concepts.text: Blocked, unsupported and not attempted are three distinct outcomes: an external precondition prevented the attempt, the path has no implementation, or no attempt was made.

concepts.section: Evidence labels used in this edition
concepts.text: The labels are coordinates, not a single quality ladder: a compile probe can answer an API question a screenshot cannot, and a hostile-input test and a pixel oracle exercise different contracts.
tokens: coordinates, not rungs of one ladder

concepts.section: Evidence labels used in this edition
concepts.text: Repository paths and revisions are the primary references instead of a bibliography; source locations describe the pin and names plus revision identifiers are the durable reproduction route.
concepts.note: Book citation policy; the site applies the same idea through TARGET-pinned source links without line anchors.

concepts.text: The pdfLaTeX pipeline does not produce a tagged PDF, so no PDF/UA conformance is claimed.
concepts.note: Book publishing detail with no CNA technical content.
